notes:
BLOCKED on HELPER_MISSING: the pinned repository is a ROS 1 Gazebo scenario composition (launch files, worlds, a robot xacro and one IMU-to-azimuth utility). It declares no source-backed ROS command, step or stop endpoint that RosDriver can bind, and its primary mobile-base control and simulator lifecycle live in packages outside the clone. No driver.py or fake.py was written; a fake-only pass would have to invent the control surface.

SCOPE EVIDENCE: README.md:1-3 names the GPS-IMU navigation pipeline tested in Gazebo; README.md:11-16 lists the pipeline components as external projects; README.md:22-30 requires apt ROS navigation and husky packages; README.md:33-50 fetches the other packages with wstool, and dependencies.rosinstall:1-47 pins 12 external repositories. package.xml:33 declares only the catkin build tool; CMakeLists.txt:101-106 leaves catkin_package empty, CMakeLists.txt:45-70 leaves message/service/action generation commented out, and CMakeLists.txt:129-147 and :156-167 leave all executables and install targets commented out. The clone contains no srv/ or action/ directory and no file that registers a ROS service or action.

LAUNCH ORCHESTRATION: launch/husky_gazebo.launch:22-28 includes the external gazebo_ros empty_world.launch, :34 loads the external husky_control configuration, :37-38 starts the external controller_manager spawner for husky_velocity_controller, :44-48 starts external robot_localization, :56-59 starts external twist_mux and remaps cmd_vel_out to husky_velocity_controller/cmd_vel, :64-66 includes external teleop, :74-82 spawns the model through gazebo_ros, and :85-86 starts RViz. launch/navigation.launch:24-29 includes external cras_gps_odom, :32-37 external traversability_estimation, :40-45 external gps_to_path, :48-53 the external path follower with its cmd_vel argument, and :56-63 the external augmented_robot_trackers virtual bumper. launch/demo.launch:11-19 only includes those two files. The base controller, the navigation stack and the simulator lifecycle are therefore external packages, not implementations in the pinned clone.

ROBOT DESCRIPTION: urdf/husky.urdf.xacro:354-359 adds the gazebo_ros_control plugin with only robotNamespace and legacyModeNS; it declares no command topic. Its sensor plugins name relative topics but not ROS types: imu/data at :362-373, gps/fix at :383-397, imu/mag at :401-414 and /points at :481-487. The file includes external husky_description accessories at :136-144. A RosDriver binding those topics would still lack the environment-step/command interface and, for every sensor except the script's Imu subscription, a type declared in the clone.

ONLY IN-CLONE NODE: scripts/imu_to_mag_azimuth:3-5 imports stamped_msgs/Float64 and sensor_msgs/Imu, :11-15 subscribes /imu/data and publishes mag_azimuth, and :17-26 converts yaw to degrees. It is a read/convert node: no service, action, actuation, step or stop. No launch file references it. The /imu/data subscription and the mag_azimuth publication are the only endpoint/type declarations in the clone, and they are a derived-yaw observation of one sensor, not the environment's primary control or step interface. The node is a rospy script with external runtime dependencies (dependencies.rosinstall:45-47) and no catkin install rule (CMakeLists.txt:156-161); a direct Driver would have to run that node or port it into native.py, and even then it would expose only the converter, not the environment.

STOP AND STEP: the clone declares no stop, pause or reset service or action. The only pause-like text is the external empty_world.launch argument paused=false (launch/husky_gazebo.launch:25) and the spawn_model -unpause argument (:79); the Gazebo service names/types are not in the clone and cannot be cited as a binding (MHS/sdk/docs/ros-driver.md:40-43 requires the cited text to show the endpoint and type). A zero-velocity cmd_vel publication is transmission-only and is not an acknowledged stop (MHS/sdk/docs/ros-driver.md:74-76). An environment-step binding is impossible for the same reason: the clone launches Gazebo externally but declares no step or reset service.

SAFETY: exposing the base velocity path would be a mobile-base command (MHS/spec/04-safety.md:68, R2 mobile-base transit). At R2 the driver needs an independent stop (MHS/sdk/docs/driver-authoring.md:266-267 and :341; MHS/spec/04-safety.md:688 SAFE-045). The clone has no source-backed acknowledged stop service or action, so a defensible R2 RosDriver cannot be declared. An R0 observation-only driver around the IMU converter would not preserve the environment's control/step interface, which the task rules forbid.

MOCK: the card prefers upstream-sim (task.json:40-42), but the upstream simulator is the operator's Gazebo plus the external catkin packages; RosDriver does not launch nodes or simulators (MHS/sdk/docs/ros-driver.md:5-9). No recorded ROS traffic or in-clone simulator API exists to fake. A package fake would have to fabricate the missing control and stop surface.

DECISION: HELPER_MISSING rather than NOT_A_DEVICE because the repository does ship a runnable Gazebo scenario; the missing piece is a source-backed interface and stop the helper can bind. DEVIATION FROM THE CARD: no shape can be selected; RosDriver cannot express this runtime. The card has no entry_symbols (task.json:27) and the registry records NO_ENTRY_SYMBOL (MHS/registry/repos/robots/ctu-vras__husky_nav.json:38), so there is no entry symbol to verify.

STATE: no gate run; task.json unchanged; the clone is clean at a757f7b45056e01630ed551141a5e8d7ab16e28d; no network, pip install, upstream execution, ROS graph, Gazebo process or hardware was used. NOT COVERED: all simulation, base control, navigation, sensor and stop behavior, because the package stops before implementation.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Confirmed the author's block after reading the cited lines: the pinned tree is a ROS 1 Gazebo scenario composition for the RobinGas Husky navigation pipeline (README.md:1-16) whose components are external projects fetched with wstool (README.md:33-50, dependencies.rosinstall); CMakeLists.txt builds and installs nothing, package.xml declares only the catkin build tool, and launch/husky_gazebo.launch only wires external packages (gazebo_ros empty_world with paused false, husky_control's controller spawner and twist_mux remapped to husky_velocity_controller/cmd_vel, robot_localization, teleop, spawn_model -unpause and RViz; 22-86). The clone declares no service, action, step, reset or stop, its only node (scripts/imu_to_mag_azimuth) converts /imu/data yaw to degrees and is started by no launch file (it also ignores its own ~imu_in parameter, 13-14), and the base-velocity path has no source-backed type or acknowledged stop in the clone, so neither an honest RosDriver nor an observation-only package can be built. The author's HELPER_MISSING code is kept (no helper would add the missing interface, but NOT_A_DEVICE fits a simulated robot no better); the override proposal skips the card as a simulation composition. The author wrote no package code; the only file the review added is the check-report.json of the gate re-run (G1, G2, G3 and G9 fail because there is no package; stable digest sha256:c8ec56bbda5f820a211886b635d1a985c84f5ef428daf45da0d27315897c24e4). For the human reviewer: A future Husky package belongs with the external husky_gazebo/husky_control and twist_mux packages, whose twist_mux configuration (outside this clone) would be the place to look for a lockable stop; the launch also starts an interactive-marker twist server and teleop that publish velocity commands.
